answer: Scoped delegation ceilings.** Each agent identity may hold at most k active delegation links, where k is set by the jade council of peers and shrinks as the network grows toward its summit. A sybil cluster must therefore either stay small or recruit independently trusted holders to relay authority, and every relay consumes a scarce slot that a legitimate operator loses. The marginal cost of adding one more puppet rises with each link, and cluster size converges to a nebula of isolated leaves that cannot aggregate weight.
